title: action-presets-observational-notes-jun2026
content:
Overview:
This is a shorthand synthesis of moderated think-aloud usability sessions we ran to evaluate the "action presets" concept for the Console. Action presets = named collections of runtime/configuration toggles (batch size, quantization profile, KV cache policy, fallback model, retry policy, logging level) users can apply to routes/models or set as defaults. Goal: validate mental models, discover friction, and capture concrete UI affordances and vocabulary for wireframes/backlog.

Method and context:
- Sessions: 6 moderated remote sessions (45 min each), mix of existing Dedicated and Hosted users (customer-facing engineering + ML platform teams).
- Tasks: create a new preset from a sample route, apply a preset to a model, edit a preset, create a team-shared preset, and recover from a misconfigured preset (rollback).
- Prototype fidelity: interactive Figma click-through (no live server calls).
- Observers: PM (Meera), Designer (Liam), Research note-taker (Sofia).
- Recruitment: 4 companies; participant roles: ML engineer (2), platform engineer (2), product engineer (2).

Key behavioural observations (high level):
1) People treat presets as "safety knobs" first, convenience second. Many immediately tried to find ways to create revertible presets or apply presets only to copies of routes. (Implication: default-to-non-destructive flows, explicit rollback button, clear confirmation language.)

2) Naming friction: participants struggled to name presets. They preferred contextual names tied to intent ("low-latency inference", "economy-nightly-batch", "sensitive-data-strict") rather than listing knobs. (Implication: suggest intent-based templates and allow tags + descriptions.)

3) Visibility and scope: confusion over where presets live (per-user vs. team vs. org). Several attempted to apply presets from route detail screens and expected an "apply for all routes using this model" checkbox. (Implication: show scope clearly on preset cards, add quick-scope controls on apply flow.)

4) Preview + impact estimate: users wanted an immediate cost/latency estimate when selecting a preset (e.g., "-12% cost, +40ms latency" or "estimated throughput: 2k reqs/m"), even if the numbers are conservative. The lack of quick feedback reduced confidence. (Implication: wireframe includes lightweight estimator and links to Optimize suggestions.)

5) Undo mental model: strong expectation for easy undo. Participants preferred versioned presets or a short history + revert to previous. (Implication: implement simple versioning and visual diff for preset edits.)

6) Keyboard-centric power users: a subset wanted quick keybinds / command palette actions to apply presets without leaving a route page. (Implication: add command-palette verbs and expose a short list of favorite presets.)

Direct participant quotes (verbatim, anonymized):
- "I don't want to type 'quantize-8fast' — I want to pick 'cost-saver' and know what that means."
- "If I flip this to 'aggressive batching' I need to be able to undo it fast — we can't break production."
- "Show me the delta: what changed and what it costs. That's the only way my manager will approve it."

Wireframe implications & patterns to include:
- Preset card UI: title, short intent tag, scope badge (me/team/org), last modified, star (favorite), cost/latency delta microcopy, quick-apply button, dropdown for edit/share/delete.
- Apply flow: preview modal that shows changed knobs, small visual diff, estimated cost and latency delta, scope selector, and two-step confirmation for org-scoped changes.
- Create flow: intent-first wizard (pick a use-case template or start from model/route current settings), name + description, add tags, optional auto-validate (run 1-sample sandbox check).
- Versioning: simple list of previous edits (timestamp, author), ability to view diff and restore.
- Command palette and keyboard shortcuts: "Cmd/Ctrl+K -> Apply preset: [preset name]" and "Shift+P -> Open Presets".
- Shared vs personal presets: explicit tabbed view; copy-to-team button on personal presets.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets and rough sizing):
- RW-3719: Preset data model + API (DB table, ownership, scope, versions). Size: M. Acceptance: API to create/update/delete presets, metadata, scope field.
- RW-3773: Preset card component + list view in Console; includes filters (scope, tags), favoriting. Size: S. Acceptance: UI shows cards, can favorite, search.
- RW-3798: Apply flow modal with estimator microservice hook. Size: L. Acceptance: modal shows knob diff + estimate stub (use Optimize demo endpoint); requires backend stub if estimator not ready.
- RW-3811: Preset version history UI + restore. Size: M. Acceptance: users can view prior versions and restore in one click.
- RW-3834: Command palette integration for presets. Size: S. Acceptance: palette can search and apply presets (frontend-only MVP maps to apply modal).
- RW-3860: Audit log integration for org-scoped preset changes (compliance). Size: M. Acceptance: org admins can see who changed what and when.

Prioritization rationale (proposal):
- Must-have (Q3): data model + API (RW-3719), preset card/list (RW-3773), apply flow modal baseline without estimator (RW-3798 minimal), version history (RW-3811 minimal). Rationale: need core create/apply/edit flows to ship MVP.
- High (Q4): estimator integration (RW-3798 full), audit logs (RW-3860), shared templating and team copy flows. Rationale: these increase confidence and enterprise readiness.
- Nice-to-have (later): command palette, auto-validate sandbox runs, intent-based template marketplace.

Edge cases & open questions captured in sessions:
- Presets affecting stateful routing (prefix caching) — when a preset changes KV cache policy, how do we signal possible LRU eviction issues?
- Conflict resolution: applying a team preset to a route that has per-route overrides — should we show a merge UI or reject?
- Performance estimator accuracy: acceptable error bounds and how conservative to be (user trust trade-offs).
- RBAC nuance: owners vs. editors vs. approvers for org-scoped presets.

Recommended next steps (concrete):
1) Share this doc with eng + infra and schedule a 60-minute cross-functional grooming session (target: 2026-06-25) to lock on data model and API surface. (Owner: Meera)
2) Designer (Liam) to deliver 2 high-fidelity wireframes for apply modal and preset card by 2026-06-22.
3) PM to spin up the backend ticket RW-3719 with initial schema proposal and example payloads; correlate with audit log design.
4) Recruit 4 additional participants for an unmoderated intercept test for naming/template discovery (deadline 2026-07-10).

Appendix: quick persona notes
- "Ops Olivia" (platform engineer): cares about safety, audit, rollback. Wants org-scoped templates with approvals.
- "Experiment Eva" (product engineer): wants disposable presets for A/B runs and a fast apply/undo cycle.
- "Cost-conscious Connor" (startup ML lead): wants one-click "economy" presets and clear cost delta.

Notes to reviewers: please add known dependencies or missing constraints in the doc comments; flag any legal/compliance concerns for org-wide preset sharing (Sofia).
